The ASV supplies a lexical verb and its object for a clause whose Hebrew writes neither; `added` under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause, together with the object supplied alongside it. The ASV italics corroborate this without deciding it (rule 7).
`גַם` takes the written *also*; a morpheme is present for it, so rule 51's `added` case does not arise.
Preposition takes the written *in*.

The `לְ` of `לֵאמֹר` has no English realization (rule 27).
Infinitive rendered *saying*.

review_notes: Supplied determiners: the phrase's *the*s before `שָׁנָה`, `דָּבָר`, `פֶּה` and `רוּחַ` all go to those construct nouns under rule 29, since no article morpheme stands anywhere in those chains.
The waw of `וַיַּעֲבֶר` takes the whole *so that* pair under rule 55; the alternative of heading it on *that* is noted in the unit.
*put it* is the only `added` material: rule 20 keeps a wholly supplied lexical verb and its supplied object out of the neighbouring `גַם`, `בְּ` and `מִכְתָּב` units.
